title: ProxySearch: Decoupled Inference-Time Scaling for Diffusion Models via Asymmetric Noise-Rank Transfer
claim: Cheap distilled proxies preserve rankings for simple closed-form properties but not for learned semantic scorers, and this is due to distillation.
layout: 2 stacked panels: top heatmap, bottom grouped bar charts; teal vs orange color coding
description: Panel (a) is a heatmap of proxy-to-teacher Spearman rank correlation. Rows are three diffusion backbones (FLUX, SD3.5, SDXL). Columns are eight closed-form image statistics (brightness, color temperature, compression, saturation, sharpness, contrast, colorfulness, edge density), then three learned semantic rewards (CLIP, ImageReward, aesthetic), separated by a thick vertical line. The cells use a teal-to-brown diverging scale, and the closed-form block is dark teal, with 0.80 for SD3.5 brightness. The learned-reward block is near zero (0.02–0.12) and pale. Panel (b) has two grouped bar charts, for FLUX and SD3.5. Each statistic has three bars with error bars: gray hatched raw-noise statistic, orange undistilled teacher at 1 step, and teal distilled proxy at 1 step. The y-axis is rho to the full teacher. The eye goes first to the dark teal heatmap corner.
caption: ProxySearch sets an image statistic by choosing the initial noise. Each row is one SD3.5 prompt, with the target value of one statistic increasing from left to right.
abstract: Noise search at inference time improves text-to-image diffusion but requires many multi-step teacher rollouts per query. Distilled few-step models are now routinely released, yet their potential as proxies inside noise search is uncharacterized. We measure proxy-teacher rank agreement across three distillation regimes and three backbones (DiT, MMDiT, UNet) and find a sharp asymmetry. On our main pool, closed-form image statistics transfer from the proxy to the teacher (Spearman $Ï$ up to 0.80), while learned semantic scorers do not ($Ï\le$ 0.12). Paired null controls trace this rank to the first denoising step for coarse statistics and to distillation for finer ones. We use the asymmetry for noise search under a joint constraint: a semantic reward specifies content, and a numeric target specifies image statistics. In PROXYSEARCH, the proxy filters candidates by statistical match in 1 step, and the teacher returns the survivor with the highest semantic reward. No weight trades one objective against the other. On FLUX-1024, PROXYSEARCH tightens the statistical target by 21-23% at the same number of teacher trajectories, with no detected loss on the optimized reward.
